sections.content:
14,830 people

were counted on the census as "hospital porters" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Hospital porters perform various manual tasks in hospitals to assist nursing and domestic staff with the care of patients.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "hospital porters" there were more men than women (90% compared with 10%).

This means "hospital porters" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "elementary administration and service occupations".

Men made up 90% and women made up 10% of "hospital porters"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "hospital porters" included:

  • aircraft pilots and air traffic controllers
  • delivery drivers and couriers
  • bus and coach drivers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "hospital porters" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "hospital porters", 16.6% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "hospital porters" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "hospital porters" included:

  • library clerks and assistants
  • roundspersons and van salespersons
  • sheet metal workers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "hospital porters" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "hospital porters" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "hospital porters", 11.5% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (79.7% compared with 20.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (99.2%) than self-employed (0.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
